sanity_expectations: D=0 remains an invariant state; with the supplied positive initial D, D(t) should stay nonnegative and relax toward 0 rather than crossing far through it.
recombination_rate(t) should increase monotonically from 0.3 toward its setpoint 0.55.
occupancy_buffer and refractory_occupancy should remain nonnegative for these nonnegative initial conditions and positive sensitivities/relaxation rates.
Because refractory_occupancy_relaxation_rate is much smaller than occupancy_relaxation_rate, refractory_occupancy should lag occupancy_buffer and decay more slowly after D becomes small.
The effective decay factor multiplying -D should vary over time, so log|D| versus t should show curvature rather than a single straight exponential segment.
Boundary compression and refractory suppression are active but not overwhelming at the inherited small initial D; expect mild-to-moderate modulation of decay, not deep saturation of the denominator.
role_corrections: dD_dt: claimed-output/target derivative -> derivative of dependent state D (confirmed as state RHS, not sampled independent target)
D: claimed-dynamic state -> dependent variable and dynamic state (confirmed)
recombination_rate: claimed-dynamic state -> dynamic state (confirmed by typed ODE contract / preserved freedom decision)
occupancy_buffer: claimed-dynamic state -> dynamic state (confirmed by typed ODE contract / preserved freedom decision)
refractory_occupancy: claimed-dynamic state -> dynamic state (confirmed by typed ODE contract / preserved freedom decision)
equation_type: upstream ode_system contract retained (overrides local scalar-expression explicit hint because the full provided governing contract supplies the coupled state system)
spec.rationale: Preserve the supplied typed ODE-system contract exactly: time is the only sampled axis; D is the dependent target state; recombination_rate, occupancy_buffer, and refractory_occupancy remain dynamic states per the explicit freedom-change history and must not be demoted to fixed parameters. The chosen window t in [0,25] with 300 points is long enough to show the multiscale transition structure without pushing everything into an almost-flat terminal equilibrium immediately: recombination_rate relaxes on an O(1) timescale toward a higher setpoint, occupancy_buffer responds on a similar but somewhat faster timescale to D^2, and refractory_occupancy evolves more slowly, so the same trajectory can exhibit early changing proportional decay, amplitude-dependent curvature from the nonlinear D term and boundary-compression term, and delayed extra suppression from refractory memory. Parameter values are kept within the suggested magnitudes and away from recovery limits: nonlinear_ld_coupling>0 makes per-unit-LD erosion increase with |D|, boundary_compression_strength>0 counteracts unchecked cubic steepening at larger |D|, and refractory_occupancy_strength>0 with slow refractory_occupancy_relaxation_rate introduces visible but not dominant path-dependent suppression. The initial D=0.05 is modest, so the strongest large-|D| contrasts are not activated immediately; accordingly this dataset will emphasize transient time-varying slope and mild-to-moderate memory/buffering effects rather than extreme boundary compression. No observation noise is added.

spec.scenario_text: Track linkage disequilibrium between two neutral biallelic loci while recombination acts at a fixed intensity. The marginal allele frequencies are held constant, leaving the signed allelic association as the only evolving quantity. A continuous-time approximation is used to describe the erosion of both positive and negative associations toward linkage equilibrium.

response_change.parent_relation: With a constant recombination_rate, the target mapping is dD_dt versus D as a single linear decay with one shared slope: dD_dt=-recombination_rate*D.
response_change.child_relation: Release recombination intensity from being time-constant by allowing it to relax as a state, so the target mapping becomes dD_dt=-r(t)*D with time-varying slope magnitude during the trajectory.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories observed over time with the same initial D, the parent predicts a straight line in dD_dt versus D with fixed proportionality, whereas the child predicts changing proportionality over time, visible as non-exponential decay of |D| and curvature on a semilog plot.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when recombination environment changes on comparable timescales to LD decay, so the effective recombination intensity is not approximately constant over the observation window; if recombination relaxes much faster or much slower than D, the parent may be an adequate approximation.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, mild departure from a pure exponential decay appears as time-varying proportional loss of D; in holdout, stronger or longer observations reveal clearer semilog curvature from the same mechanism.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the recombination state is constant in time, equivalently when its relaxation rate is zero or its initial value equals its steady value for all t.
plan.promotion_reason: A time-varying recombination intensity cannot be represented with the existing single fixed parameter if one must use one shared parameter set across trajectories; it needs its own ODE state to encode environmental relaxation during the experiment.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes recombination intensity is fixed through time, omitting plausible transient changes in effective recombination conditions during the observation window.
plan.baseline_assumption: The recombination intensity is constant through time.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Temporal relaxation of effective recombination intensity due to changing mating or chromosomal pairing conditions, while recombination still always erodes LD toward zero.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed-environment assumption on recombination itself rather than adding an unrelated process. Vary the observation time window and trajectories in which effective recombination conditions relax, while holding neutrality, fixed marginal allele frequencies, and absence of mutation/migration/drift/selection unchanged. The parent enforces one exponential decay shape for D(t) with a single constant proportional slope for all times. The child allows that proportional slope to change during the run as recombination_rate evolves, producing curvature in log|D| versus t and a non-constant dD_dt/D. This is a changed target mapping, not merely auxiliary complexity, because the scored derivative of D directly depends on the evolving recombination_rate. The effect is admissible so long as recombination_rate remains nonnegative, ensuring dD_dt always points toward zero and D=0 stays invariant. Limitation: if the effective recombination intensity is nearly constant over the sampled interval, the refinement will not be distinguishable from the parent.

contract.scientific_mechanism: Temporal relaxation of effective recombination intensity due to changing mating or chromosomal pairing conditions, while recombination still always erodes LD toward zero.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding introduces a distinct recombination-relaxation timescale that directly modulates the scored D dynamics, producing non-exponential decay and a time-varying proportional loss rate rather than a coefficient-only rescaling of one fixed exponential.
contract.assumption_before: The recombination intensity is constant through time.
contract.assumption_after: The effective recombination intensity is an internal state that relaxes toward a setpoint during the experiment.
contract.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when recombination_relaxation_rate=0 or when the initial recombination_rate equals recombination_setpoint, making recombination_rate constant for all t.
contract.observable_signature: With the same initial D and one shared parameter set, the parent gives a single exponential D(t) and constant dD_dt/D, while the child gives time-varying dD_dt/D and curvature in log|D| versus t whenever recombination_rate starts away from recombination_setpoint and relaxes on a comparable timescale.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted constant parent recombination_rate can match only one effective proportional decay slope, not the within-trajectory drift in dD_dt/D generated when recombination_rate itself relaxes over time. Across observation windows where that relaxation is visible, one shared parent parameter set cannot reproduce both early-time and late-time decay behavior.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping is dD_dt = -recombination_rate*D, so for any observed recombination_rate the decay magnitude is a single linear gain in |D| with constant local slope -recombination_rate.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the strictly linear erosion law with a bounded odd dependence on D so the effective decay gain decreases as |D| approaches its admissible maximum, while retaining the sign toward zero. Then dD_dt remains zero at D=0 and opposite in sign to D, but the |D|->|dD_dt| relation becomes curved rather than purely linear.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed observed recombination_rate, small |D| still decays approximately exponentially, but larger |D| decays more slowly than the linear parent predicts, producing state-dependent curvature in D(t) and a smaller-than-linear magnitude of dD_dt at high |D|.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories sample a non-negligible range of |D|, especially moderate-to-large |D| relative to its feasible scale; effect is weak near D=0 where the child must reduce to the parent approximately.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest |D| already shows near-zero versus moderate-|D| differences in effective decay gain; in holdout, larger |D| extends this same curvature, with stronger attenuation of decay magnitude than any single linear gain can match across all sampled states.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the weak-association limit where |D| is small compared with its saturation scale, so the nonlinear erosion factor linearizes to 1.
plan.promotion_reason: A saturation scale is needed to express when finite feasible haplotype constraints begin to blunt the proportional erosion of LD. Existing symbols provide only D and a time-varying recombination_rate, which cannot by themselves encode a separate internal measure of available recombinantizable association without collapsing back to a refit linear gain.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes recombination removes a fixed fraction of LD per unit time regardless of how close the association is to the maximal values permitted by fixed allele frequencies.
plan.baseline_assumption: The loss of association is exactly proportional to D over the full admissible range.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite-haplotype occupancy can limit the amount of association that is effectively available to be broken down, making recombination-driven erosion saturate at large |D| even though it still points toward linkage equilibrium.
plan.rationale: Vary the observed state D along trajectories while holding the recombination-rate relaxation parameters fixed. In the parent, once recombination_rate is given, the target mapping from D to dD_dt is a single straight line through the origin with slope -recombination_rate. A realistic refinement is that at larger |D|, finite feasible haplotype occupancy reduces the marginal amount of further recombinant breakup available, so the decay magnitude grows sublinearly with |D|. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely the auxiliary recombination_rate trajectory, because two times with the same recombination_rate but different |D| would have different normalized decay gains in the child and identical gains in the parent. The contrast is scientifically admissible when initial or transient LD is not infinitesimal; near D=0 the refinement should become hard to distinguish and recover the parent approximately. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the near-origin slope and the attenuated large-|D| decay across one dataset spanning those conditions, because its D-to-dD_dt map remains exactly linear for all D.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer, the target mapping is linear in D: dD_dt = -(recombination_rate/(1+occupancy_buffer))*D, so the erosion strength per unit |D| is independent of |D| once the auxiliary states are given.

response_change.observable_effect: At matched recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer, small |D| decays nearly as before but larger |D| decays disproportionately faster, producing a curved relationship between |D| and |dD_dt| that the parent's single gain cannot match over both weak- and strong-LD portions of the same trajectory.

contract.parent_reduction: Taking boundary_compression_strength -> 0 removes the geometric compression term and recovers the parent expression exactly.
contract.observable_signature: Holding recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer fixed, the child agrees with the parent to leading order near D=0 but shows reduced growth of |dD_dt| at larger |D| because the effective erosion coefficient is divided by 1 + occupancy_buffer + boundary_compression_strength*D**2. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely auxiliary state trajectories.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both moderate-amplitude steepening and large-amplitude flattening across the same admissible D range. Refitting nonlinear_ld_coupling only globally increases or decreases cubic amplification; it cannot introduce the child’s opposing high-|D| compression while preserving similar mid-range erosion under the same recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer conditions.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer, dD_dt is an odd monotone function of D whose magnitude changes with |D| only through a single rational dependence on D**2, so positive and negative associations with the same |D| decay with the same one-phase shape.
response_change.child_relation: Retain decay toward zero but relax the assumption that the occupancy limitation responds instantaneously with one linear relaxation mode; introduce a slowly accumulating refractory occupancy memory so the effective erosion at a given current |D| depends on recent prior |D| exposure, changing the local curvature of the D-to-dD_dt mapping during sustained large-|D| episodes versus transient ones.
response_change.observable_effect: Two trajectories that pass through the same current D can show different |dD_dt| depending on whether they arrived after prolonged high |D| or after a brief excursion; sustained high |D| yields stronger temporary suppression of erosion than the parent can produce from current D alone.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when |D| remains moderately large for times comparable to or longer than the occupancy response timescale, so a slow occupancy-refractory component can separate sustained from transient exposure; weak near D≈0 or under very rapid passage through low |D|.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, trajectories with different recombination_rate relaxation histories can generate the same instantaneous D but different recent high-|D| dwell times; in holdout, the same memory mechanism extends this contrast to longer sustained episodes and larger occupancy buildup.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the refractory occupancy contribution is absent or relaxes infinitely fast so the additional memory collapses into the existing occupancy_buffer response.
plan.promotion_reason: A genuine history-dependent occupancy refractory effect cannot be represented by refitting existing algebraic D dependence or the single occupancy_buffer state, because those make dD_dt at a given current state depend only on present D and present buffer, not on an additional slow hidden occupancy phase created by past sustained LD.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes a single-timescale occupancy limitation, so all suppression of recombinational erosion is determined by one buffer that relaxes linearly toward a D**2 target.
plan.baseline_assumption: Occupancy limitation is fully captured by one fast linear relaxation variable slaved to current D**2, with no slower refractory or crowding-memory phase.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Sustained excess occupancy of overrepresented haplotypes can leave a slower refractory crowding state that continues to limit effective recombinant reshuffling even after instantaneous LD has already begun to relax, while still preserving decay toward D=0.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the one-phase occupancy assumption rather than add an unrelated process. In the parent, if current D, recombination_rate, and occupancy_buffer are the same, then dD_dt is fixed; any two trajectories intersecting the same state have identical target dynamics. That is a single-phase shortcut. Biologically, finite haplotype occupancy can have a slower refractory component: prolonged strong association can leave persistent crowding or access limitation beyond the fast buffer. Vary the duration of prior large-|D| exposure while holding the current observed D and the fixed parameters comparable; under admissible conditions with sustained moderate-to-large |D|, the child can produce temporarily smaller |dD_dt| after long exposure than after a brief excursion, whereas the parent with one shared parameter set cannot because its target mapping is Markov in the existing state tuple and has no extra memory. This changes the scored target mapping, not merely an auxiliary trajectory, provided the new slow state enters the D equation. The effect should remain weak near D=0 and disappears in the limit of vanishing or infinitely fast refractory occupancy, which cleanly recovers the parent.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite capacity, resource limitation, or saturation

baseline_mechanisms: Recombination breaks apart associated allele combinations and creates alternative haplotypes.
The loss of association is proportional to the association currently available to be broken down.
baseline_assumptions: The recombination intensity is constant through time.
Marginal allele frequencies at both loci are fixed.
The loci are neutral, and the population mates randomly.
Mutation, migration, drift, gene conversion, and epistatic selection are absent.
scientific_constraints: The change rate must always point toward zero linkage disequilibrium.
Zero linkage disequilibrium is an invariant state.
Linkage disequilibrium must remain within bounds compatible with valid haplotype frequencies.
refinement_agenda: Allow the marginal allele frequencies to evolve jointly.
Add epistatic selection that generates allelic association.
Include gene conversion as an additional association-breaking process.
Introduce migration carrying haplotypes with external linkage disequilibrium.
Extend the system to associations among more than two loci.

response_change.parent_relation: With a constant recombination_rate, the target mapping is dD_dt versus D as a single linear decay with one shared slope: dD_dt=-recombination_rate*D.
response_change.child_relation: Release recombination intensity from being time-constant by allowing it to relax as a state, so the target mapping becomes dD_dt=-r(t)*D with time-varying slope magnitude during the trajectory.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories observed over time with the same initial D, the parent predicts a straight line in dD_dt versus D with fixed proportionality, whereas the child predicts changing proportionality over time, visible as non-exponential decay of |D| and curvature on a semilog plot.

diagnostic_groups.name: signed_decay_flux
diagnostic_groups.role: instantaneous pull of linkage disequilibrium toward zero under the parent law

diagnostic_groups.name: log_decay_rate
diagnostic_groups.role: effective proportional erosion rate when D is nonzero

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when recombination environment changes on comparable timescales to LD decay, so the effective recombination intensity is not approximately constant over the observation window; if recombination relaxes much faster or much slower than D, the parent may be an adequate approximation.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, mild departure from a pure exponential decay appears as time-varying proportional loss of D; in holdout, stronger or longer observations reveal clearer semilog curvature from the same mechanism.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the recombination state is constant in time, equivalently when its relaxation rate is zero or its initial value equals its steady value for all t.
evolution_contracts.promotion_reason: A time-varying recombination intensity cannot be represented with the existing single fixed parameter if one must use one shared parameter set across trajectories; it needs its own ODE state to encode environmental relaxation during the experiment.
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Temporal relaxation of effective recombination intensity due to changing mating or chromosomal pairing conditions, while recombination still always erodes LD toward zero.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This embedding introduces a distinct recombination-relaxation timescale that directly modulates the scored D dynamics, producing non-exponential decay and a time-varying proportional loss rate rather than a coefficient-only rescaling of one fixed exponential.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The recombination intensity is constant through time.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: The effective recombination intensity is an internal state that relaxes toward a setpoint during the experiment.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when recombination_relaxation_rate=0 or when the initial recombination_rate equals recombination_setpoint, making recombination_rate constant for all t.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: With the same initial D and one shared parameter set, the parent gives a single exponential D(t) and constant dD_dt/D, while the child gives time-varying dD_dt/D and curvature in log|D| versus t whenever recombination_rate starts away from recombination_setpoint and relaxes on a comparable timescale.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted constant parent recombination_rate can match only one effective proportional decay slope, not the within-trajectory drift in dD_dt/D generated when recombination_rate itself relaxes over time. Across observation windows where that relaxation is visible, one shared parent parameter set cannot reproduce both early-time and late-time decay behavior.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping is dD_dt = -recombination_rate*D, so for any observed recombination_rate the decay magnitude is a single linear gain in |D| with constant local slope -recombination_rate.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the strictly linear erosion law with a bounded odd dependence on D so the effective decay gain decreases as |D| approaches its admissible maximum, while retaining the sign toward zero. Then dD_dt remains zero at D=0 and opposite in sign to D, but the |D|->|dD_dt| relation becomes curved rather than purely linear.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed observed recombination_rate, small |D| still decays approximately exponentially, but larger |D| decays more slowly than the linear parent predicts, producing state-dependent curvature in D(t) and a smaller-than-linear magnitude of dD_dt at high |D|.

diagnostic_groups.name: signed_decay_gain
diagnostic_groups.role: Instantaneous effective erosion rate when D != 0

diagnostic_groups.name: ld_magnitude
diagnostic_groups.role: Strength of allelic association determining proximity to admissible LD bounds

diagnostic_groups.name: normalized_flux
diagnostic_groups.role: Deviation from the parent's constant-unit linear decay gain

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories sample a non-negligible range of |D|, especially moderate-to-large |D| relative to its feasible scale; effect is weak near D=0 where the child must reduce to the parent approximately.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest |D| already shows near-zero versus moderate-|D| differences in effective decay gain; in holdout, larger |D| extends this same curvature, with stronger attenuation of decay magnitude than any single linear gain can match across all sampled states.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the weak-association limit where |D| is small compared with its saturation scale, so the nonlinear erosion factor linearizes to 1.
evolution_contracts.promotion_reason: A saturation scale is needed to express when finite feasible haplotype constraints begin to blunt the proportional erosion of LD. Existing symbols provide only D and a time-varying recombination_rate, which cannot by themselves encode a separate internal measure of available recombinantizable association without collapsing back to a refit linear gain.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: competition between recombination-driven LD erosion and finite-occupancy limitation
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Finite-haplotype occupancy can limit the amount of association that is effectively available to be broken down, making recombination-driven erosion saturate at large |D| even though it still points toward linkage equilibrium.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: The added internal state creates a history-dependent attenuation of the decay gain, so the same observed recombination_rate can produce different dD_dt values depending on accumulated occupancy limitation. This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the target map is no longer a single line in D with one shared gain.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The loss of association is exactly proportional to D over the full admissible range.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: Finite-haplotype occupancy builds an internal limitation state that competes with recombination and reduces effective erosion at larger |D|.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when occupancy_sensitivity->0 or occupancy_relaxation_rate is fast while D remains small enough that occupancy_buffer≈0.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: Vary the observed state D along trajectories while holding the recombination-rate relaxation parameters fixed. In the parent, once recombination_rate is given, the target mapping from D to dD_dt is a single straight line through the origin with slope -recombination_rate. In the child, two times with the same observed recombination_rate but different |D| can have different normalized decay gains because occupancy limitation suppresses erosion, so larger |D| shows smaller-than-linear |dD_dt|. This target-mapping contrast is observable when trajectories include moderate-to-large |D| under the stated initial-condition contract; near D=0 the refinement becomes hard to distinguish and approximately recovers the parent.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the near-origin slope and the attenuated large-|D| decay across one dataset spanning those conditions, because its D-to-dD_dt map remains exactly linear for all D once recombination_rate is specified. Changing only the auxiliary recombination_rate trajectory is insufficient because the scored contrast compares observations with the same recombination_rate but different occupancy-driven attenuation.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer, the target mapping is linear in D: dD_dt = -(recombination_rate/(1+occupancy_buffer))*D, so the erosion strength per unit |D| is independent of |D| once the auxiliary states are given.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the strictly linear dependence on D by a steeper odd restoring law whose effective erosion per unit |D| increases with |D| while preserving the sign toward zero, e.g. a nonlinear dependence on D within the recombination term moderated by the same occupancy factor.
response_change.observable_effect: At matched recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer, small |D| decays nearly as before but larger |D| decays disproportionately faster, producing a curved relationship between |D| and |dD_dt| that the parent's single gain cannot match over both weak- and strong-LD portions of the same trajectory.

diagnostic_groups.name: parent_effective_gain

diagnostic_groups.name: normalized_decay

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories sample a broad enough range of |D| away from zero so that moderate-to-large LD states occur before occupancy_buffer fully relaxes; near D=0 the child should reduce to approximately linear erosion.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the same mechanism appears as mild curvature in |dD_dt| versus |D| at moderate LD; in holdout, trajectories reaching larger |D| amplify this curvature, revealing faster-than-linear recombinational erosion that the parent cannot capture with one shared gain.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the nonlinear correction scale is sent to zero strength, restoring proportional decay dD_dt ∝ -D.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: Amplitude-dependent recombinational erosion of linkage disequilibrium
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: At stronger disequilibrium, the excess of overrepresented haplotypes can make recombinant production of counterbalancing haplotypes scale more than linearly with association amplitude in a continuous approximation, while still always driving D toward zero and leaving D=0 invariant.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This refinement changes the conditional target law itself by coupling the recombination process jointly to D and the existing occupancy-moderated rate factor, creating observable curvature in dD_dt versus D at fixed supplied auxiliary states. A coefficient-only correction would merely rescale the parent straight line and would not reproduce magnitude-dependent per-unit decay.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: Recombination-driven LD erosion is exactly proportional to D once modulated by occupancy buffering.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: Recombination-driven LD erosion increases with LD amplitude through a nonlinear odd correction while preserving the same buffering structure and equilibrium at D=0.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: Setting nonlinear_ld_coupling = 0 gives the parent expression exactly.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: Holding recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer fixed, the parent predicts a straight-line relation between dD_dt and D, whereas the child predicts near-origin linearity with progressively steeper decay at moderate |D| due to the multiplicative D-dependent correction. This contrast is observable when trajectories span both weak and moderate LD within admissible haplotype bounds before occupancy_buffer fully masks the effect.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the near-zero slope and the stronger moderate-|D| decay at the same supplied recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer because its conditional mapping from observed states to dD_dt has only one linear gain in D. Refitting existing recombination or occupancy parameters changes only that gain or auxiliary trajectories, not the required curvature in the target mapping under matched supplied states.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer, the target mapping is an odd monotone product in D with one cubic correction: dD_dt = -recombination_rate*D*(1 + nonlinear_ld_coupling*D**2)/(1 + occupancy_buffer), so the per-unit-LD erosion strength changes smoothly with D**2 but has no special compression near the admissible LD bounds.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that the available recombinant erosion scales with raw signed LD amplitude alone; instead let erosion weaken as D approaches its allele-frequency-compatible boundary, producing an additional state-dependent curvature in the D to dD_dt map even when recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer are held fixed.
response_change.observable_effect: At moderate |D| the child can match the parent's initial erosion, but as |D| moves toward larger admissible values the child predicts a flatter increase in |dD_dt| than the parent's cubic-amplified law, while still keeping the sign toward zero.
